source: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide for Non-compartmental Analysis Input Data v1.0 (Final, 2021-11-29)

dataset_metadata.structure: One record per subject per parameter per analysis visit per analysis timepoint
dataset_metadata.cdisc_notes: Dataset designed to support NCA. Primarily sourced from SDTM PC and supplemented by information from the EX, EC, or other relevant domains.

variables.label: PK NCA Exclusion Flag
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Flag for exclusion of a record into a PK NCA calculation (Y = exclusion, Null = inclusion). Codelist: Y.

variables.label: PK NCA Exclusion Flag (N)
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Numeric flag for exclusion of a record into a PK NCA calculation (1 = exclusion, Null = inclusion). NCAXFN can only be included if NCAXFL is also included. Codelist: 1.

variables.label: Reason w for PK NCA Exclusion
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: This variable is used to explain why the record is not included in the PK NCA. The 'w' represents a sequence number (e.g., NCA1XRS, NCA2XRS, NCA3XRS).

variables.label: Reason for PK NCA Exclusion of w (N)
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Numeric version of reason why the record is not included in the PK NCA.

variables.label: PK Summary Exclusion Flag
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Flag for exclusion of a record from a PK summary (1 = exclusion, Null = inclusion). Codelist: Y.

variables.label: PK Summary Exclusion Flag (N)
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Numeric flag for exclusion of a record from a PK summary (1 = exclusion, Null = inclusion). PKSUMXFN can only be included if PKSUMXFL is also included. Codelist: 1.

variables.label: Metabolite Flag
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Flag to designate if observations within a subject are associated with a metabolite. Required if parent drug and metabolites are present in the dataset. Codelist: Y.

variables.label: Subject Cohort
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Relevant to trials where cohorts are defined. This could be another grouping not necessarily associated with ARM.

variables.label: Subject Cohort (N)
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Numeric representation of the COHORT variable. There must be a one-to-one mapping between COHORT and COHORTN. When both present, on a given record either both must be populated or both must be null.

variables.label: Route
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Route of treatment delivery. Can be a copy of EX.EXROUTE or EC.ECROUTE. May instead be derived. Codelist: (ROUTE).

variables.label: Planned Treatment Interval
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Planned time between 2 consecutive treatments in multiple-dose studies (sometimes referred to as 'Tau').

variables.label: Planned Treatment Interval Units
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Units associated with TRTRINT. Codelist: (UNIT).

variables.label: Percent Diff. Nominal vs. Actual Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Derived variable using standard percent difference formula: (100*(DOSEA-DOSEP)/(DOSEP)). DOSPCTDF is required if both DOSEA and DOSEP are populated.

variables.label: Dose Frequency
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Usually expressed as the number of repeated administrations of DOSE within a specific time period for multiple dose studies. Codelist: (FREQ).

variables.label: Analysis Cycle
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Record-level identifier that reflects cycle; important for oncology studies. One-to-one mapping with ACYCLEC required. When both present, either both populated or both null.

variables.label: Analysis Cycle (C)
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Character representation of ACYCLE. Text characterizing which analysis cycle the record belongs to. One-to-one mapping with ACYCLE required. When both present, either both populated or both null.

variables.label: First Date of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Date of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE for a subject in a study where multiple doses have been given. May not match TRTSDT or TRxxSDT values.

variables.label: First Time of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Time of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. If treatment is given over a duration multiple times, reflects the start time of the first dose.

variables.label: First Datetime of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Date and time of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. If treatment given over a duration multiple times, reflects start date and time of first dose.

variables.label: First End Date of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: End date of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. May not match TRTEDT or TRxxEDT values.

variables.label: First End Time of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: End time of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. If treatment given over a duration multiple times, reflects end time of first dose.

variables.label: First End Datetime of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: End date and time of first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. If treatment given over a duration multiple times, reflects end date and time of first dose.

variables.label: Reference Date of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Date of reference exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. Based on PC.PCRFTDTC and related to the analyzed profile. If treatment over time, typically the start of the dosing duration.

variables.label: Reference Time of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Time of reference exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. Based on PC.PCRFTDTC. If treatment over time, typically the start of the dosing duration.

variables.label: Reference Datetime of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Date and time of reference exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. Based on PC.PCRFTDTC. If treatment over time, typically the start of the dosing duration.

variables.label: Reference End Date of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: End date of reference exposure to treatment. Must be related to PC.PCRFTDTC. If dosing occurs over an interval, this should be populated. If populated, ADOSEDUR and DOSEDURU are required.

variables.label: Reference End Time of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: End time of reference exposure to treatment. Must be related to PC.PCRFTDTC. If dosing occurs over an interval, this should be populated. If populated, ADOSEDUR and DOSEDURU are required.

variables.label: Ref. End Datetime of Dose for Analyte
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: End date and time of reference exposure to treatment. Must be related to PC.PCRFTDTC. If dosing occurs over an interval, this should be populated. If populated, ADOSEDUR and DOSEDURU are required.

variables.label: Nom. Rel. Time from Analyte First Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Planned elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. For extended duration infusion, use define to document if from start or end.

variables.label: Act. Rel. Time from Analyte First Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Actual elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from first exposure to treatment associated with PARAM and ANALYTE. Refers to first dose available for a particular drug; useful in multiple-dosing.

variables.label: Nom. Rel. End Time from First Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Planned elapsed end time of sampling interval from first exposure to study treatment.

variables.label: Act. Rel. End Time from First Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Actual elapsed end time of sampling interval from first exposure to study treatment.

variables.label: Rel. Time from First Dose Unit
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Unit for all elapsed times from first dose. Codelist: (PKUNIT).

variables.label: Nominal Rel. Time from Ref. Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Planned elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from reference exposure to study treatment.

variables.label: Actual Rel. Time from Ref. Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Actual elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from reference exposure to study treatment.

variables.label: Modified Rel. Time from Ref. Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Could be used to modify ARRLT based on analysis needs (e.g., setting negative values to zero or having a mix of nominal and actual time based on TMPCTDF).

variables.label: Nominal Rel. End Time from Ref. Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Planned elapsed end time of sampling interval from reference exposure to study treatment.

variables.label: Actual Rel. End Time from Ref. Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Actual elapsed end time of sampling interval from reference exposure to study treatment.

variables.label: Modified Rel. End Time from Ref. Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Could be used to modify AERRLT based on analysis needs (e.g., setting negative values to zero or having a mix of nominal and actual time based on TMPCTDF).

variables.label: Rel. Time from Ref. Dose Unit
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Unit for all elapsed times from reference dose. Codelist: (PKUNIT).

variables.label: Percent Diff. Nominal vs. Actual Time
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Percent difference between nominal and actual time. Derived using standard percent difference formula: 100*(NRRLT - ARRLT)/(NRRLT).

variables.label: Actual Duration of Treatment Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Total treatment duration in DOSEDURU units, derived from PCRFEDTM-PCRFDTM. Generally associated with infusion dose. Distinct from TRTDURD/TRTDURM/TRTDURY which reference entire study duration.

variables.label: Nominal duration of Treatment Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Nominal treatment duration as specified in protocol, in DOSEDURU units. Generally associated with infusion dose.

variables.label: Duration of Treatment Dose Units
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Units associated with ADOSEDUR and NDOSEDUR. When ADOSEDUR is present, NDOSEDUR and/or DOSEDURU must also be included. Codelist: (PKUNIT).

variables.label: Analysis Value Unit
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Unit for AVAL.

variables.label: Specimen Material Type
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Defines the type of specimen used for a measurement (e.g., SERUM, PLASMA, URINE). Must be a direct copy of PC.PCSPEC. Codelist: (SPECTYPE).

variables.label: Character Result/Finding in Std Format
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Character results/findings in standard format. Purpose is to capture which records are BLQ or LLOQ in the AVAL column. Must be a direct copy of PC.PCSTRESC.

variables.label: Standard Units
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Standardized unit associated with AVAL. Units associated with AVAL are needed for clear NCAs. Must be a direct copy of PC.PCSTRESU. Codelist: (UNIT).

variables.label: Analysis Lower Limit of Quantitation
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Indicates lower limit of quantitation for an assay. Use if PC.PCLLOQ does not support analysis needs.

variables.label: Lower Limit of Quantitation
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Indicates lower limit of quantitation for an assay. Must be a direct copy of PC.PCLLOQ.

variables.label: Volume Value
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: PC.PCSTRESN from a PC volume record. Volume related to AVAL. Conditionally required if sample is interval-based collection, such as urine.

variables.label: Volume Value Unit
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: PC.PCSTRESU from a PC volume record. Conditionally required if VOLUME is present. Codelist: (UNIT).

variables.label: Specimen Weight Value
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: PC.PCSTRESN from a PC specimen weight record, adjustment based on LLOQ rules possible. Conditionally required if sample is interval based collection such as a non-fluid matrix (e.g., feces).

variables.label: Specimen Weight Value Unit
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: PC.PCSTRESU from a PC weight record. Conditionally required if SPWEIGHT is present. Codelist: (UNIT).

variables.label: Group ID
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: Used to tie together a block of related records. Must be a direct copy of PC.PCGRPID.

variables.label: Sequence Number
variables.section: Table 4.2.1 - New Standard Non-compartmental Analysis Variables
variables.guidance: PC.PCSEQ associated with AVAL.

variables.label: Actual Treatment Dose
variables.section: Table 4.2.2 - Standard BDS Variables with Stronger Core for NCA
variables.guidance: Represents the actual treatment dosage associated with the record. This is the actual numeric amount of the dose used for NCA analysis and may differ from EX.EXDOSE. Core strengthened from BDS Perm to NCA Req.

variables.label: Treatment Dose Units
variables.section: Table 4.2.2 - Standard BDS Variables with Stronger Core for NCA
variables.guidance: Units for DOSEP and DOSEA. Permissible to use suffixes such as 'P' and 'A' to record different units for DOSEP and DOSEA, with labels modified accordingly. Codelist: (UNIT). Core strengthened from BDS Perm to NCA Req.

variables.label: Analysis Visit
variables.section: Table 4.2.2 - Standard BDS Variables with Stronger Core for NCA
variables.guidance: Analysis visit description; required if analysis is done by nominal, assigned, or analysis visit. AVISIT is derived and does not have to map to SDTM VISIT. Should be unique for a given analysis visit window. Core strengthened from BDS Cond to NCA Req.

conformance_rules.description: ADNCA follows the ADaM BDS (Basic Data Structure).
Dataset structure: One record per subject per parameter per analysis visit per analysis timepoint.
Class is BASIC DATA STRUCTURE, SubClass is NON-COMPARTMENTAL ANALYSIS.
NCAXFN can only be included if NCAXFL is also included.
PKSUMXFN can only be included if PKSUMXFL is also included.
METABFL is required if parent drug and metabolites are present in the dataset.
There must be a one-to-one mapping between COHORT and COHORTN. When both present, on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.
DOSPCTDF is required if both DOSEA and DOSEP are populated. Formula: 100*(DOSEA-DOSEP)/(DOSEP).
There must be a one-to-one mapping between ACYCLE and ACYCLEC. When both present, on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.
PCRFEDT, PCRFETM, PCRFEDTM: If dosing occurs over an interval, these should be populated. If populated, ADOSEDUR and DOSEDURU are required.
TMPCTDF is derived using formula: 100*(NRRLT - ARRLT)/(NRRLT).
ADOSEDUR is derived from PCRFEDTM - PCRFDTM.
When ADOSEDUR is present, NDOSEDUR and/or DOSEDURU must also be included in the dataset.
PCSPEC must be a direct copy of PC.PCSPEC.
PCSTRESC must be a direct copy of PC.PCSTRESC.
PCSTRESU must be a direct copy of PC.PCSTRESU.
PCLLOQ must be a direct copy of PC.PCLLOQ.
PCGRPID must be a direct copy of PC.PCGRPID.
VOLUME is conditionally required if sample is interval-based collection (e.g., urine).
VOLUMEU is conditionally required if VOLUME is present.
SPWEIGHT is conditionally required if sample is interval-based collection from a non-fluid matrix (e.g., feces).
SPWEIGHU is conditionally required if SPWEIGHT is present.
DOSEA, DOSEU, and AVISIT have stronger core (Req) for NCA than in general BDS use.
Select ADSL Permissible variables are Required in ADNCA because they are scientifically necessary to support PK analyses.
PARAM should completely describe the value in AVAL, including units and specimen type (if applicable).
When a record is duplicated for analysis purposes (e.g., 24h post-dose doubles as next-period pre-dose), DTYPE must be populated (e.g., 'COPY') and PCSEQ is repeated.
Baseline units for NCA characteristics (BMIBL, HTBL, WTBL) are stored in separate variables (BMIBLU, HTBLU, WTBLU) rather than in the label, due to NCA tool requirements.
Usage of start and end datetimes in nominal or actual relative time calculation needs to be described in the define.
AVISIT should be unique for a given analysis visit window. Values and derivation rules may differ for different parameters within the same dataset.
ADNCA datasets should be 'analysis-ready' containing all variables needed for performing NCA.
Excluded records should still be included in the dataset for traceability and consistent reporting, with NCAXFL set to 'Y' and appropriate NCAwXRS reason populated.
For extended duration infusions, use the define to document whether NFRLT is measured from start or end of infusion.
